modern_module_boundary.axiom_profile_context: The separate existing CollectAxioms review records precomputed imported axiom summaries and export-time collection. It is not a reason to remove or replace the actual named #print axioms gate.
modern_module_boundary.current_graph_blocker: A modern root rejects direct legacy imports, even import all. An unchanged legacy final root forces importAll recursively and therefore reintroduces the private data of modern intermediates. A one-file modern wrapper around the unchanged current graph is not a solution.
modern_module_boundary.decision: No one-file or small-wrapper production fix preserving this graph and all existing byte-bound origins is established. A 75-module pilot is a bounded future feasibility study, not a fix for this run; the 25k closure migration is outside this task.
modern_module_boundary.existing_supported_mechanism: Modern module serialization separates exported/server/private data; importing at exported level can use a reduced public ConstantInfo interface rather than the private theorem bodies. The standard module system, rather than manual axiom replacement or object rewriting, is the relevant supported mechanism.
modern_module_boundary.production_gate_implications: Changing source/module visibility would require genuine recompilation and newly bound source/closure/member provenance. Existing legacy archives cannot be relabeled as reduced modern exports. Public signature visibility and the standard named axiom reports must be demonstrated unchanged; no imported theorem may be substituted by a newly asserted axiom.
modern_module_boundary.sidecar_mapping_limit: The default filesystem loader opportunistically loads available modern parts. Selecting exported constant data is not by itself a promise that no private sidecar is mapped.

smallest_previously_bounded_pilot.status: Structural bound only; no modernization implementation or compile test

concrete_integration_boundaries: Do not plan GDB and strace as simultaneous ptrace tracers of the same Lean tracee. A debugger-parent design would replace the active ptrace wrapper for that diagnostic step and needs its own verified timeout/owned-child cleanup behavior.
A perf-based alternative needs an actual availability/permission/unwind check for the owned child; no assumption of usable perf_event access and no kernel/sysctl or resource-limit change.

Any future wrapper must first pass a small real owned-child control, retain the exact Lean command and 900-second/one-worker/2048-MiB/host-reserve policy, and archive raw samples with transparent observer overhead.
No full core dump or proof-object rewrite is needed for the stated stack-observation goal.

static_import_path_findings.fact: A legacy source selects global private import level and calls importModules with loadExts=true before returning its environment and processing later source commands. Zero flushed source markers therefore leaves this full pre-command region open; it does not identify a subroutine.

A failed saved-address mapping falls back synchronously to malloc/readn and region_reader. A legacy main region has no passed dependency regions; a successful saved-address mapping can return the saved root without a full structural fixup walk. The slow path walks compacted objects, but that work is inside loading, not the later constant-map loop.
static_import_path_findings.limit: This static route does not identify the long observed post-mapping phase, nor prove that all proof-body pages are subsequently read.

static_import_path_findings.fact: finalizeImport selects ModuleData and IR data for all imported modules, counts constants, preallocates maps, iterates each constNames/constants pair, inserts Name-to-ConstantInfo references and Name-to-ModuleIdx entries, then includes extraConstNames. These accesses span imported arrays and name/hash data in compacted regions. The legacy root skips the separate isModule public-map loop.
static_import_path_findings.proof_value_traversal: No general call to ConstantInfo.value or an expression/proof traversal occurs in this loop. Loading a reference or object header is different from traversing its full proof body.

static_import_path_findings.fact: subsumesInfo is invoked on duplicate names. It compares names, types and level parameters, then theorem all metadata or permitted axiom/theorem forms. The source explicitly excludes equality of theorem value fields. Type equality and the cheap proposition check can still traverse type expressions.
static_import_path_findings.limit: This is not evidence that actual duplicate-name checking dominates the run.

static_import_path_findings.fact: The concrete name-to-declaring-module map in this pin is const2ModIdx. No identifier importedConstModules occurs in the four fully captured source files; a separate full-proof traversal under that requested name is not established.

setImportedEntries sizes per-extension arrays by module count and walks each module extension table, retaining its entry arrays. finalizeImport prepares ordinary, IR and server extension views. finalizePersistentExtensions then calls every registered addImportedFn, runs init attributes at the designated point, and can discover more extensions/attributes. The callbacks may inspect their imported entries or use the environment.
static_import_path_findings.limit: The generic path does not enumerate which concrete extension callbacks or expression fields were touched in this failed run. It does not justify assuming every imported proof value is recursively visited.

static_import_path_findings.fact: When leakEnv is true, finalizeImport invokes Runtime.markPersistent before extension initialization and again afterwards. The serialized compacted objects have non-heap headers; EnvironmentHeader documents that they need no memory management.
static_import_path_findings.limit: The Runtime.markPersistent implementation and the concrete CLI leakEnv caller are not among the four fully captured files. This review does not claim that markPersistent traverses all compacted proof bodies or that it was the measured long-running function.
